findings.passage: What I’ve said very clearly from the start in my work over the years to address gun laws in our community to protect our cities, working across Kentucky, as a director of Fish and Wildlife, I want us to fully fund community and public safety.
findings.note: Interview transcript on WBKO; he says he has worked on gun laws to protect cities and wants community safety funded. No specific policy named.
subjects: general statement on gun safety laws

findings.note: HB 70 would make it a crime to store a firearm unsafely, including letting a minor reach an unsecured firearm (safe storage). Listed as a co-sponsor/sponsor on the legislature's bill page.

HB 76 would define assault weapons, large-capacity magazines and bump stocks, require background checks for private gun sales, require reporting of lost or stolen guns, require safe storage, and ban making, selling or transferring bump stocks. Listed as a co-sponsor/sponsor on the legislature's bill page.

HB 376 would let people petition a district court for one-year extreme risk protection orders to remove firearms from a person judged a significant danger (red-flag orders). Listed as a co-sponsor/sponsor on the legislature's bill page.

HB 31 would repeal KRS 237.109, the law allowing concealed deadly weapons to be carried without a license. Booker is listed first among the sponsors (primary sponsor). Date is the prefiling date. Listed as a co-sponsor/sponsor on the legislature's bill page.
subjects: carry a gun without a permit

findings.note: HB 45 would define assault weapons and large-capacity magazines, require background checks for private gun sales, require safe storage and theft reporting, and require licensing of handgun and assault weapon owners. Date is the prefiling date. Listed as a co-sponsor/sponsor on the legislature's bill page.
